key_insight: Epidemic forecasts that ignore strategic misreporting of self-reported behaviors can be systematically biased; jointly modeling user deception and epidemiological dynamics yields more robust state estimates and safer forecasts under adversarial data.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap where self-reported behavioral data (vaccination, masking, distancing) are strategically manipulated by users, causing biased epidemic forecasts and misleading policy guidance. The paper provides a framework to detect, model, and mitigate the impact of adversarial reporting on transmission estimates.
method: Formulate a joint model that couples epidemiological state dynamics with a behavioral/adversary model capturing incentives and misreporting strategies.
Develop robust inference and estimation algorithms (e.g., adversarial-aware filtering, reweighting or game-theoretic estimation) to recover true population-level signals from corrupted self-reports.
Evaluate mitigation strategies and forecast corrections to quantify improved resilience of predictions under varied deception scenarios.
impact: Enables ML and public-health practitioners to produce more reliable epidemic forecasts and policy evaluations when input data may be strategically manipulated, improving the trustworthiness of AI-driven interventions during outbreaks.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram linking users (with incentives), reported behavioral signals, an adversary model, and the epidemiological simulator/state estimator.
Comparison chart of forecast trajectories: naive model vs. adversarial-aware model, showing error reduction and uncertainty bands.
Flowchart of the pipeline: data ingestion → deception detection/reweighting → joint inference → robust forecasting.
Icon set representing common incentives (e.g., penalties, access benefits, distrust) to illustrate why users misreport.
paper_title: Modeling Epidemiological Dynamics Under Adversarial Data and User Deception
paper_authors: Yiqi Su, Christo Kurisummoottil Thomas, Walid Saad, Bud Mishra, Naren Ramakrishnan
